chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wasshash who said:

I heard Al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the sun passes its zenith (Zawal) and you are in the city (Masr), and you intend to travel, then complete (the four rak'ahs of) the Dhuhr prayer; and when you depart after Zawal, shorten (to two rak'ahs) the Asr prayer.'

key_terms.اَلزَّوَالِ: The passing of the sun from its zenith, marking the beginning of Dhuhr time
key_terms.اَلْمِصْرِ: The city or place of residence

ai.seo_question: How to shorten prayers when traveling after Zawal?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Al-Rida (AS) clarifies the specific timing for the transition from full to shortened prayers during travel, establishing that the Dhuhr prayer remains complete if the intention to travel arises after the sun has passed its zenith. It highlights the practical application of the 'Qasr' rule, ensuring travelers maintain ritual integrity by distinguishing between the stationary state (in the city) and the traveling state (after departure).
